findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate docs/adr/0069 (and any dependent ADR enumerating the retryable vocabulary, e.g. 0077) as an edit-set consumer, since low-disk's distinct terminal no-vote disposition diverges from ADR 0069's documented 'all retryable reasons vote at exhaustion' invariant.
evidence: docs/adr/0069-retryable-coverage-gap-bounded-deferral.md:16 references `adapter.RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS` and its vote-at-exhaustion model
docs/adr/0077-code-review-voter-four-pass-rewire.md:45 enumerates `<gate-disabled|llm-unavailable|scanner|review-error>` as the coverage-gap tag vocabulary

Plan text: 'it must have a distinct terminal disposition: when the low-disk retry budget is exhausted, leave Gerrit labels unchanged and emit/log a no-vote deferral/exhaustion result rather than posting the fail-closed LLM-Review -1'
File impact lists docs/review-policy.md and passing-code-review.md but no ADR
findings.finding: The plan changes ADR 0069's documented retryable-gap invariant (all RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS cast a fail-closed -1 once the budget is exhausted) by giving low-disk a distinct terminal no-vote/labels-unchanged disposition, but neither docs/adr/0069-retryable-coverage-gap-bounded-deferral.md nor docs/adr/0077-code-review-voter-four-pass-rewire.md (both of which enumerate the retryable gap-reason vocabulary and the exhaustion-vote invariant) is listed in File impact.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify WHERE the low-disk terminal fork lives (e.g. a `gap_reason == 'low-disk'` branch inside _handle_retryable_gap, taken BEFORE the append_retries_exhausted_note/_voter_error/-1 exhaustion branch) so an exhausted low-disk budget returns a no-vote/labels-unchanged deferral result and NEVER reaches the fail-closed -1 + VOTER_ERROR path that review-error/llm-unavailable/scanner/gate-disabled use.
evidence: Plan: 'it must have a distinct terminal disposition: when the low-disk retry budget is exhausted, leave Gerrit labels unchanged and emit/log a no-vote deferral/exhaustion result rather than posting the fail-closed LLM-Review -1 used for real review errors.'
Plan: 'Add low-disk to ... RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS ... then route it through ADR 0069's existing _handle_retryable_gap machinery.'

voter.py:437-451 — the exhaustion branch of _handle_retryable_gap calls append_retries_exhausted_note, fires _voter_error(...vote_value=cfg.llm_review_block_value...), and returns (decision, None), after which _review_and_vote (voter.py:670-725) maps BLOCK→llm_review_block_value and POSTs the fail-closed -1.

Ticket 0347 comments confirm the exhaustion path was deliberately built to '-1 + CloudWatch metric' for review-error/llm-unavailable/scanner/gate-disabled — the disposition low-disk must diverge from.
findings.finding: Routing `low-disk` through the existing _handle_retryable_gap machinery (by adding it to RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS) sends its budget-exhaustion case into that function's existing terminal branch, which casts the fail-closed LLM-Review -1 and fires VOTER_ERROR — the exact behaviour the plan says low-disk must NOT have. The plan requires a distinct terminal disposition but does not name where the low-disk fork lives to divert exhaustion away from the -1/VOTER_ERROR path.
findings.location: Approved design → Part B, paragraph beginning 'low-disk is an infrastructure admission refusal'; against src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:_handle_retryable_gap (lines 387-451)
scenarios: An acute-disk-pressure host defers a review low-disk N times; on the Nth attempt the unchanged _handle_retryable_gap escalates to a spurious LLM-Review -1, re-introducing the very fail-closed infra-veto this ticket exists to eliminate.
The retrigger/reconciler recovery then treats the change as already-voted (-1) and stops re-driving it, requiring a human — the closed-ticket failure class 2731/9bc0 recurring.
findings.suggested_fix: State that _handle_retryable_gap gains an explicit low-disk arm: while under budget it defers vote-less exactly like other retryable gaps; at/over budget it returns a distinct {status:'deferred-exhausted', gap_reason:'low-disk'} (no vote POST, no label write, no VOTER_ERROR escalation — an emit/log-only exhaustion marker), leaving the existing exhaustion branch untouched for the genuine coverage-gap reasons.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the exact literal low-disk _TAG_SUFFIXES string (e.g. 'BLOCK — coverage-gap (low-disk)' matching the plan's own '[LLM-Review deferred: coverage-gap (low-disk)]' example) and state whether it must satisfy retrigger._GAP_RE or requires a new grammar branch in classify_tag.
evidence: Plan: 'Add low-disk to ... _TAG_SUFFIXES' and 'a documented low-disk tag suffix' but no literal value is given.
Plan: 'low-disk is an infrastructure admission refusal, not a code coverage gap.'
adapter.py:64-73 _TAG_SUFFIXES entries all use the form 'BLOCK — coverage-gap (<reason>)'.

retrigger.py:80 _GAP_RE = '^BLOCK — coverage-gap \((?P<reason>[a-z][a-z-]*)\)$' — classify_tag returns 'coverage-gap:<reason>' only for strings matching that grammar; a suffix outside it classifies as 'unparseable'.
findings.finding: The plan mandates 'a documented low-disk tag suffix' and adding low-disk to _TAG_SUFFIXES, but never defines the literal suffix string, and its 'not a code coverage gap' framing leaves ambiguous whether the suffix must follow the existing 'BLOCK — coverage-gap (<reason>)' grammar.
findings.location: Part B — near-full review admission control; Acceptance Criteria bullet 6
scenarios: Executor adds a _TAG_SUFFIXES['low-disk'] value that does not match _GAP_RE, so retrigger.classify_tag returns 'unparseable' and the reconciler/retrigger path mishandles the deferral.
Two implementers pick different suffix strings, breaking the documented-vocabulary test.
findings.suggested_fix: Define _TAG_SUFFIXES['low-disk'] = 'BLOCK — coverage-gap (low-disk)' so it parses under the existing _GAP_RE grammar, and confirm retrigger.classify_tag needs no new stem; if the deferral message uses the plan's alternate '[LLM-Review deferred: ...]' prefix instead of '[LLM-Review: ...]', specify the corresponding classify_tag/_TAG_LINE_RE extension.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the explicit decision rule that gives low-disk its distinct terminal disposition — how _handle_retryable_gap branches on gap_reason at budget exhaustion so low-disk emits a no-vote/labels-unchanged exhaustion result instead of the append_retries_exhausted_note + fail-closed -1 taken by other RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS members.
evidence: Plan: 'route it through ADR 0069's existing _handle_retryable_gap machinery. Add low-disk to ... RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS'.
Plan: 'when the low-disk retry budget is exhausted, leave Gerrit labels unchanged and emit/log a no-vote deferral/exhaustion result rather than posting the fail-closed LLM-Review -1'.

voter.py:437-451 _handle_retryable_gap: on budget spent it calls append_retries_exhausted_note + _voter_error(vote_value=cfg.llm_review_block_value) and returns deferred_result=None so the caller casts the fail-closed -1 — this fires for ALL RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS members with no per-reason branch.
findings.finding: The plan routes low-disk through the existing _handle_retryable_gap machinery and adds it to RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS, yet demands a distinct terminal (no-vote) disposition on budget exhaustion — but the existing machinery unconditionally casts the fail-closed -1 for every RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS member on exhaustion, so the required decision rule that branches disposition by gap_reason is never specified.
findings.location: Part B — 'route it through ADR 0069's existing _handle_retryable_gap machinery' and 'distinct terminal disposition'; Acceptance Criteria bullet 4
scenarios: An executor adds low-disk to RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS and reuses _handle_retryable_gap unchanged; on exhaustion the bot casts LLM-Review -1 for low-disk, directly violating AC bullet 4.
The exhaustion-disposition branch key (gap_reason == 'low-disk' vs a separate LOW_DISK set) is left to implementer guess.
findings.suggested_fix: State whether low-disk joins RETRYABLE_GAP_REASONS or a separate set, and add an exhaustion-branch rule: if gap_reason == 'low-disk', skip append_retries_exhausted_note and the block-value _voter_error, emit a distinct no-vote exhaustion log/result, and return deferred_result so the caller casts no vote; keep the existing -1 path for all other reasons.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that an ENOSPC/No-space error surfacing during the clone/materialization AFTER a passing free-space admission check is mapped to the retryable low-disk deferral (gap_reason=low-disk, no-vote terminal) and NOT to the fail-closed review-error -1, closing the check-then-act residual window.
evidence: Plan: 'Check the target volume before both relevant materialization paths ... If the target volume is below the floor, do not start the clone.'

Absence: no statement that an ENOSPC surfacing AFTER a passing admission check maps to gap_reason=low-disk / no-vote deferral rather than VOTER_ERROR review-error; the original incident IS ENOSPC during clone.
findings.finding: The admission check is a check-then-act against a live disk: free space is measured (shutil.disk_usage), then the clone starts. Under acute pressure the volume can cross below the floor (or ENOSPC) between the check and the clone/materialization, and the plan does not state that the residual ENOSPC on the clone path still degrades to the retryable low-disk deferral rather than the fail-closed LLM-Review -1 it is trying to eliminate.
findings.location: Part B — near-full review admission control; AC 'aborts before clone ... rather than ENOSPC'
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC and design note: wrap the clone/materialization in an ENOSPC handler that re-routes to the same low-disk retryable/no-vote disposition as the pre-clone admission floor.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that REBAR_GATE_MIN_FREE_GIB is a best-effort pre-clone floor (a point-in-time shutil.disk_usage read that concurrent clones and the clone-in-progress can still overrun), and that a clone which ENOSPCs despite passing the check falls through to the existing review-error retryable path — so admission control reduces but does not eliminate ENOSPC.
evidence: Plan: 'If the target volume is below the floor, do not start the clone.' and AC: 'aborts before clone ... rather than ENOSPC'.

shutil.disk_usage(path) is a point-in-time read; the voter runs reviews concurrently (voter.py _in_flight accounting, multiple TemporaryDirectory clones on the same root volume), so free space measured pre-clone is not the free space during the clone.
The residual ENOSPC still surfaces as a GerritError in voter.py:653-664 → review-error, which is already retryable — so the floor DEGRADES gracefully, but the plan does not say so.
findings.finding: The near-full admission check is a check-then-act on free space (shutil.disk_usage read, then start the clone), which is a coarse best-effort floor rather than an ENOSPC guarantee: the clone itself and concurrent reviews consume space after the check, so a clone larger than the residual headroom above the 2 GiB floor can still ENOSPC. The plan presents the floor as if it prevents ENOSPC ('aborts before clone ... rather than ENOSPC') without acknowledging the residual race or the fallback when a clone ENOSPCs despite passing the check.
findings.location: Approved design → Part B; Acceptance Criteria line 'snapshot materialization aborts before clone with a retryable low-disk condition rather than ENOSPC'
scenarios: Free space is 2.5 GiB (above the 2 GiB floor) but the change's clone needs 1 GiB and two other reviews are cloning concurrently → ENOSPC despite passing admission control.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether Part A (autodeploy reclaim) and Part B (review admission control) should ship as one leaf or as two children, given they are independently valuable and touch heterogeneous subsystems (shell deploy vs Python gate).
evidence: Part A lives in infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh (host deploy shell); Part B lives in src/rebar/review_bot/*, _snapshot/*, llm/gate_source.py (Python gate logic).
Structural 'and': 'The operator approved BOTH parts'; the two parts have distinct proofs and distinct test suites.
findings.finding: The ticket bundles two independently-releasable outcomes touching heterogeneous subsystems: Part A (emergency BuildKit reclaim tier in infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh + shell/prune tests) and Part B (Python review-bot admission control, ADR 0069 retry routing, snapshot guard, docs). Each is independently valuable and shippable — reclaim reduces disk pressure regardless of admission control, and admission control prevents fail-close regardless of reclaim.
findings.location: Approved design — Part A and Part B; File impact
